items.title: A Busy Morning in Marrakesh
items.summary: Layla visits the old market in Marrakesh, buys a blue rug for her mother and enjoys mint tea.
items.body: Layla arrived in Marrakesh on a hot Friday morning. She wanted to buy presents for her family, so she walked to the old market. The market was full of colours and smells. A friendly man showed her silver lamps and soft rugs. Layla chose a small blue rug because her mother loved blue things. She paid twenty euros and the man smiled. Then she drank cold mint tea at a little cafe and watched the people go by. She felt happy and tired at the same time, and she decided to come back next year.

words.def: a place where people buy and sell things

items.title: Omar Learns to Swim
items.summary: Omar is afraid of water, but with his father's help he learns to swim one summer in Cairo.
items.body: Omar was seven years old and he was afraid of water. Last summer his father took him to a swimming pool in Cairo every Saturday. At first Omar only put his feet in the water. His father stayed close and said, Don't worry, I am here. Slowly Omar started to put his face under the water. After five lessons he could float on his back. At the end of the summer he swam across the small pool, and everyone clapped. Now Omar wants to join the school swimming team next year.

items.title: Emma's Small Vegetable Garden
items.summary: Emma grows tomatoes, carrots and beans in her Toronto garden and cooks a salad for her friends.
items.body: Emma lives in a small house in Toronto with a big garden. In April she planted tomatoes, carrots and beans. Every morning before work she checked the plants and pulled out the weeds. Her neighbour Tom gave her advice because he grew vegetables for many years. In July the tomatoes were red and ready. Emma picked a full basket and cooked a big salad for her friends. The carrots were small but very sweet. Next spring she wants to plant peppers too, and maybe some strawberries for her little sister.

words.def: a place next to a house for plants

items.title: Ken Finds a Lost Kitten
items.summary: Ken finds a wet kitten outside his flat in Osaka, cares for it and finds its owner online.
items.body: One rainy evening, Ken heard a small sound outside his flat in Osaka. He opened the door and found a wet kitten under the stairs. The kitten was cold and hungry, so Ken carried it inside and dried it with a towel. He gave it some warm milk and a little fish. The kitten ate everything and then slept on his sofa. The next morning Ken asked his neighbours about the kitten, but nobody knew it. Ken put a photo on the internet. Two days later, a happy girl came to take her cat home.

items.title: Fatou's First Day at Work
items.summary: Fatou starts a job at a hotel in Dakar, serving breakfast to guests, and feels proud at the end.
items.body: Fatou got a job at a hotel near the beach in Dakar. On her first day she woke up very early and put on her new uniform. Her manager showed her the kitchen and the big dining room. Fatou's job was to bring breakfast to the guests. She was nervous, but the guests were kind and said good morning with a smile. One guest asked for fresh orange juice, and Fatou remembered it quickly. At five o'clock her manager said, Well done. Fatou went home by bus, tired but proud of her first day.

items.title: A Long Bicycle Ride
items.summary: Marco rides his bicycle from Lisbon to a fishing village, eats grilled fish and enjoys his best Sunday.
items.body: Marco loves his old bicycle more than his phone. Last Sunday he rode from his home in Lisbon to a small fishing village by the sea. The road went up a long hill, and his legs hurt, but he did not stop. At the top he saw the ocean and took a deep breath. In the village he ate grilled fish and drank lemon water. On the way back the wind pushed him, so the ride was easier. He arrived home at six, dirty and smiling. It was his best Sunday this year.

words.def: a machine with two wheels for riding

items.title: Amina Sees Snow in London
items.summary: Amina from Khartoum sees snow for the first time in London and builds a snowman with her cousin.
items.body: Amina grew up in Khartoum, where it never snows. Last December she visited her aunt in London, and on the second morning the streets were white. Amina ran outside in her warm coat and caught snowflakes on her hands. They felt cold and disappeared fast. Her little cousin showed her how to make a snowball, and they built a small snowman in the park with a carrot nose. Amina took many photos to send to her mother. That night she wrote in her diary, Today was the most beautiful day of my life.

items.title: The School Science Fair
items.summary: Priya and Grace test plants in sun and dark for the science fair and win second prize.
items.body: Priya and her classmate Grace worked on a project about plants for the school science fair. They put one plant in a sunny window and one in a dark cupboard. They watered both plants the same amount every day. After two weeks, the plant in the sun was tall and green, but the plant in the dark was yellow and weak. Priya wrote the results on a big poster, and Grace practised the presentation at home. On Friday, the judge gave their project second prize. The girls were very excited and celebrated with ice cream.

items.title: Kofi's Day on a Fishing Boat
items.summary: Kofi helps his uncle on a fishing boat in Tema, catches fish and a boot, and sells them at market.
items.body: Kofi's uncle has a small fishing boat in Tema, a town by the sea. Last Saturday Kofi woke up at four in the morning to help him. The sky was still dark when they left the harbour. They threw their nets into the quiet water and waited. An hour later, they pulled the nets up. There were fish, a crab and one old boot! The uncle laughed loudly. They sold most of the fish at the morning market, and Kofi's uncle gave him some money for his help. On the way home, they ate fried fish by the beach.

items.title: Mei Makes Dumplings
items.summary: Mei learns to make dumplings with her grandmother in Seoul and makes better ones than her teacher.
items.body: Every Friday, Mei cooks dinner with her grandmother in their small kitchen in Seoul. This week they made dumplings. First, grandmother mixed flour and water to make the dough. Then Mei cut vegetables and meat into small pieces. Her grandmother taught her to fold each dumpling with her fingers. Mei's first dumpling looked strange and fat, but her last one looked perfect. They cooked the dumplings in hot water and ate them with soy sauce. Grandmother said Mei's dumplings tasted better than hers. Mei smiled all evening because she learned something new.

items.title: Ivan's New Flat in Istanbul
items.summary: Ivan moves to a small flat in Istanbul with a lovely view, buys curtains and invites his brother.
items.body: Ivan moved to a new flat in Istanbul last month. The flat is small, but it has a big balcony with a view of the old city. From there he can see the sea and the boats. The best thing is the location: the market, the bakery and the bus stop are all two minutes away. The worst thing is the noise in the morning, because the street is busy. Ivan bought thick curtains and now he sleeps better. He invited his brother for dinner next weekend to show him the view.

items.title: Zola Runs Her First Race
items.summary: Zola trains for six months in Sydney, changes her habits and finishes her first ten kilometre race.
items.body: Six months ago, Zola could not run for five minutes. Then she decided to change. She started with short runs around her neighbourhood in Sydney, two or three times a week. Slowly the runs became longer. She drank more water, went to bed earlier and ate better food. Her friend Ivan ran with her on weekends and always said, Keep going, you can do it. Last month Zola finished a ten kilometre race in the city park. Her time was not fast, but she did not care. She already signed up for a longer race.

items.title: Yuki Saves for a New Phone
items.summary: Yuki breaks her phone screen, saves money for three months and buys a simple phone with her own money.
items.body: Yuki dropped her phone on the stairs, and the screen broke. A repair shop wanted a lot of money, so she decided to save for a new one. She put part of her pocket money in a box every week. She also washed her neighbour's car and helped in her aunt's shop on Saturdays. After three months she counted the money in the box. It was enough! Yuki bought a simple phone with a good camera. It cost less than the expensive one, but she paid with her own money, and that felt wonderful.

items.title: A Night in the Desert
items.summary: Guide Khaled takes visitors on a desert trip with camels, tents, stars and a sunrise behind the rocks.
items.body: Khaled works as a guide in the desert near a small town in Jordan. Last week he took a group of visitors on a two day trip. They rode camels across the orange sand and slept in tents. At night the sky was full of bright stars, and Khaled showed the group the different shapes. He cooked rice and chicken on a small fire, and everyone said it was the best dinner of the trip. In the morning they watched the sunrise behind the rocks. The visitors promised to come back with their families.

items.title: The Storm by the Lake
items.summary: Elena's family picnic by the lake is interrupted by a storm, but a rainbow appears and the day ends well.
items.body: Elena and her family were having a picnic near the lake, when the sky suddenly turned dark. The wind blew the paper plates off the blanket, and big raindrops started to fall. Everyone ran to the car, laughing and shouting. Then they heard a loud sound of thunder, and Elena's little brother started to cry, so she held his hand and told him a funny story. After twenty minutes the rain stopped, and a beautiful rainbow appeared over the lake. They drove home with wet shoes, but everyone agreed it was an exciting afternoon.

words.def: a meal eaten outside in nature

the loud sound after lightning

items.title: Jack Visits Doctor Silva
items.summary: Jack feels tired and has headaches, so Doctor Silva gives him advice that makes him much healthier.
items.body: Jack often felt tired and had headaches, so he went to see Doctor Silva. She asked about his food and his sleep. Jack told her that he ate fast food almost every day and went to bed after one in the morning. Doctor Silva said, Your body needs better habits. She told him to walk thirty minutes a day, drink more water and eat fruit between meals. Jack followed her advice. After six weeks he felt stronger, and the headaches disappeared. Now he cooks simple meals at home and sleeps before eleven, and he feels much healthier.

items.title: Sofia Looks for a Winter Coat
items.summary: Sofia finds a warm blue coat at half price in a Madrid sale and buys a scarf and gloves too.
items.body: Winter was coming, so Sofia went to the shopping centre in Madrid to find a warm coat. The first shop had beautiful coats, but they were too expensive. In the second shop she found a nice blue coat in the sale. It was half price because the shop wanted to sell the old collection. Sofia tried it on, and it fit perfectly. She also bought a red scarf and warm gloves with the money she saved. On the bus home, she felt happy. Now she is ready for the cold months, and she still has money left.

items.title: Tom's Uncle Visits from Canada
items.summary: Tom's uncle visits from Canada for three weeks, tells farm stories and promises to teach Tom to fish.
items.body: Last spring, Tom's uncle came from Canada to visit the family for three weeks. Tom had not seen him since he was six years old. His uncle brought maple sweets and hundreds of photos. Every evening the family sat in the garden, and the uncle told stories about his life on a farm: cold winters, big forests and funny animals. Tom asked a lot of questions and wrote some answers in a notebook. On the last day, the uncle promised to teach Tom how to fish when he visits Canada one day. Tom counted the days already.

items.title: A Quiet Island Holiday
items.summary: Layla and her friend enjoy a car free Greek island with swimming, books under olive trees and free fish.
items.body: Last summer Layla and her best friend travelled to a small island in Greece. There were no cars on the island, so they walked everywhere or used old bicycles. Their room was simple, with a bed, a table and a window that looked at the sea. Every morning they swam in the clear blue water before breakfast. In the afternoons they read books under an olive tree. The people in the village were friendly, and one old fisherman gave them fresh fish for free. When the holiday ended, Layla cried a little on the boat.

words.def: land with water all around it
machines with two wheels for riding

items.title: Amina's Weekend Job at a Bookshop
items.summary: Amina works at a bookshop on Saturdays, helps customers and saves money for a photography course.
items.body: Amina found a weekend job at a small bookshop in her town. On Saturdays she opens the shop at nine, arranges the books and helps the customers. Many older people come and ask for books about history or gardens. Amina likes to recommend her favourite stories to young readers. The owner pays her at the end of the day, and she saves most of the money for a photography course. Last month a customer left a kind note that said, Thank you for your help. items.title: Grace Joins the Coding Club

items.body: Every Tuesday after school, Grace goes to the coding club in the library. Last month the teacher showed the class how to make a simple game. At first Grace's little cat on the screen did not move at all. She checked her instructions again and found a missing word. When she fixed it, the cat jumped across the garden and caught an apple. Everyone clapped, and Grace laughed happily. Now she wants to build a game about space for her younger brother. Her teacher says the club will start an advanced group next term.

items.title: A Surprise Snow Day
items.summary: Heavy snow closes Priya's school, so she plays outside, drinks hot chocolate and plays a board game.
items.body: Priya woke up and looked out of the window. Everything was white and very quiet. The radio said all schools were closed because of heavy snow. Priya and her brother put on warm clothes and ran into the garden. They made a snowman, threw snowballs and slid down the small hill behind the house. Their mother called them in for hot chocolate with marshmallows. Their wet gloves dried near the fire while they played a board game together. Priya wrote in her diary that snow days are the best days of the winter.

items.title: The School Cooking Competition
items.summary: Omar cooks his grandmother's lentil soup in a school competition and wins a cookbook and a gold sticker.
items.body: Omar's school had a cooking competition before the holidays. Omar decided to make lentil soup, because his grandmother taught him the recipe. He chopped onions and carrots and added cumin and lemon. The kitchen smelled wonderful. One competitor burned his rice, and another forgot the salt, but Omar stayed calm and followed each step. The judges tasted every dish slowly. At the end, the head teacher announced the winner: Omar! He won a cookbook and a gold sticker for his class. He called his grandmother immediately to tell her the good news.

items.title: Tom Helps at an Animal Shelter

items.body: Every Sunday morning, Tom takes the bus to an animal shelter outside the town. There are about forty dogs and fifty cats there. Tom fills the water bowls, cleans the cages and plays with the young dogs in the garden. His favourite is a brown dog called Biscuit, who was found alone near the river. Last month a family adopted Biscuit, and Tom felt sad and happy at the same time. The shelter manager says volunteers like Tom are very important, because the animals need love and exercise, not only food.

items.title: Meeting a New Neighbour

items.title: Interesting Facts about Camels
items.summary: Camels survive long desert journeys because they store fat in their humps and drink very fast.
items.body: Camels are large animals that live in hot, dry places like deserts. They can travel for many days without drinking water, because their bodies store fat, not water, in their humps. A camel can drink about one hundred litres of water in ten minutes. Camels have long eyelashes and they can close their noses to keep sand out. Their wide feet help them walk on soft sand without sinking. People use camels to carry heavy things and sometimes for their milk. Because of all these special abilities, people call camels the ships of the desert.

items.title: How Bees Make Honey
items.summary: Bees collect nectar from flowers, turn it into honey in the hive and help plants grow fruit.
items.body: Bees are small insects, and they do a very important job. They fly from flower to flower to collect a sweet liquid called nectar. They carry the nectar back to their home, which is called a hive. Inside the hive, many bees work together and turn the nectar into honey. Bees store the honey in six sided wax rooms called cells, and they eat it during the winter. One hive can make more than twenty kilos of honey in a good year. Farmers also like bees because they help plants grow fruit.

items.title: Why We See Rainbows
items.summary: Rainbows appear when sunlight passes through rain drops and its hidden colours separate into a curve.
items.body: A rainbow appears in the sky when sunlight and rain happen at the same time. The light from the sun looks white, but it is really made of many colours. When sunlight passes through drops of rain, the colours separate, and we see red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple in a big curve. A rainbow always appears on the opposite side of the sky from the sun. That is why rainbows are easiest to see in the morning or in the late afternoon, when the sun is low.

items.title: Rice: Food for Millions
items.summary: Rice grows in warm wet fields, comes in thousands of kinds and gives people energy every day.
items.body: Rice is one of the most important foods in the world. Billions of people eat it every day, especially in Asia. Rice grows in warm, wet places, and farmers often plant it in special fields covered with shallow water. These green fields are beautiful, like mirrors. There are thousands of kinds of rice, with different sizes, colours and tastes. People cook rice in many ways: they boil it, fry it or grind it into flour for noodles and sweets. Rice gives the body energy, so in many countries it is eaten with every meal.

items.title: Visiting Your Local Library
items.summary: Libraries lend free books, keep local history and offer quiet corners, computers and librarians to help.
items.body: A library is a place full of books that people can borrow for free. In most libraries you can also read newspapers, use a computer or study in a quiet corner. Libraries keep old maps, photos and documents, so they are important for local history. Many libraries have a special children's area with picture books and story times. If you want to take a book home, you need a library card, which is usually free. When you finish the book, you return it, and someone else can enjoy it. Librarians are always happy to help you find something.

items.title: Why Sleep Is Important
items.summary: Sleep repairs the body, saves new memories, and most adults need seven to nine hours every night.
items.body: Sleep is very important for a healthy body and mind. While you sleep, your body repairs itself and your brain saves the new things you learned during the day. Most adults need about seven to nine hours of sleep every night, and children need even more. People who do not sleep enough often feel tired, angry or sad, and it is harder to remember things. A good habit is to go to bed at the same time every night. Before sleeping, it helps to turn off bright screens and drink a warm, calm drink like milk.

items.title: The World's Most Popular Sport
items.summary: Football needs only a ball and two stones for goals, with two teams of eleven playing ninety minutes.
items.body: Football is the most popular sport on earth. Millions of people play it, and billions watch the big international competitions on television. The rules are simple: two teams of eleven players try to kick the ball into the other team's goal. Only the goalkeeper can touch the ball with his hands. A normal match lasts ninety minutes, with a short break in the middle. Children can play football almost anywhere, because all they need is a ball and two stones for goals. This is one reason why the game is loved in every country.

items.title: The Story of the Bicycle
items.summary: Early bicycles had no pedals, but today over a billion bicycles give people a cheap and healthy ride.
items.body: The bicycle is one of the most useful machines ever invented. The first machines with two wheels appeared in Europe about two hundred years ago, but they had no pedals. Riders pushed the ground with their feet, like on a scooter. Later, inventors added pedals, better wheels and brakes, and the modern bicycle was born. Today there are more than one billion bicycles in the world, far more than cars. In many cities people ride bicycles to work because they are cheap, healthy and good for the environment. Cycling also keeps your heart strong.

items.title: Life of the Penguins
items.summary: Penguins cannot fly but swim with flipper wings, eat fish and huddle together in the freezing wind.
items.body: Penguins are birds, yet they cannot fly. Instead, they are excellent swimmers, and they use their wings like flippers to move fast under the water. Most penguins live in the cold south of the planet, but some live in warm places too. Penguins eat fish and small sea animals. They often stand together in big groups to stay warm in the freezing wind. Emperor penguins, the largest kind, can dive deeper than five hundred metres. Both the mother and the father penguin help to keep their egg warm until the baby hatches.

items.title: Where Coffee Comes From
items.summary: Coffee beans are roasted seeds of a fruit, and Brazil grows more coffee than any other country.
items.body: Coffee is one of the most popular drinks in the world. Coffee beans are the seeds of a fruit that grows on small trees in warm countries. The beans are picked, dried and then roasted, which turns them brown and gives them their famous smell. Brazil grows more coffee than any other country. People drink coffee in different ways: in some places it is very strong and small, and in other places it is served with milk and sugar. Many people say they cannot start the day without a cup of coffee.

items.title: Why the World Has Time Zones
items.summary: The earth turns, so the world is divided into time zones, and flying east usually means losing hours.
items.body: When it is morning in one country, it can be night in another country far away. This is because the earth turns, and the sun lights only one half at a time. To make clocks useful, the world is divided into areas called time zones. Countries inside one zone use the same time. When you fly east, you usually lose hours, and when you fly west, you gain them. Without time zones, a plane landing in a far country would arrive before it left! Modern smartphones change the time automatically when you travel.

items.title: Cold and Hot Deserts
items.summary: Deserts simply get very little rain; Antarctica is the biggest one, and cactuses store water in stems.
items.body: Many people think deserts are always hot, but this is not true. A desert is simply a place with very little rain, so some deserts are actually cold. The largest hot desert is the Sahara in Africa, but the biggest desert of all is Antarctica, which is covered with ice. Days in hot deserts can be extremely warm, yet nights are often cold, because there are no clouds to keep the heat. Some plants, like cactuses, store water inside their thick stems. Many desert animals only come out at night when the air is cooler.

items.title: Interesting Facts about Salt
items.summary: Salt once kept food fresh and workers were paid with it; today it comes from the sea or the ground.
items.body: Salt is one of the oldest and most useful things in the kitchen, but it has a bigger story. Long ago, before fridges, people used salt to keep fish and meat fresh for months. Salt was so valuable that in some places workers were even paid with it. The word salary comes from an old word for salt. Today most salt comes from the sea or from deep holes in the ground. Our bodies need a small amount of salt to work well, but doctors say too much salt is bad for the heart.

items.title: What Is a Volcano
items.summary: Volcanoes let hot lava escape; active ones can erupt, and scientists watch them carefully to keep people safe.
items.body: A volcano is an opening in the surface of the earth where hot liquid rock can escape from inside. This hot liquid rock is called lava when it flows out. Some volcanoes are active, which means they can wake up and erupt again. Others have been quiet for thousands of years. When lava cools down, it becomes hard, dark rock, and after many eruptions a mountain grows higher and higher. The soil around old volcanoes is very rich, so farmers often grow food on the green slopes. Scientists watch active volcanoes carefully to keep people safe.
